newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae group continues to seek meeting.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae group continues to seek meeting.

text.p: A dissident shareholder group said Friday it is continuing its attempt to call a special meeting of shareholders of Student Loan Marketing Association and believes modified proposals from the Sallie Mae board do not offer a "real choice" to shareholders.
Earlier Friday, Sallie Mae said its board approved modifications to corporate governance proposals on which shareholders will vote at a special meeting May 15.

The new Sallie Mae proposals call for annual election of all holding company directors instead of a staggered board and for elimination of all supermajority requirements. By eliminating supermajority requirements, holders of one third of the outstanding shares could call a special meeting, and at such a meeting any directors could be replaced by a majority vote with or without cause.
Ronald Mueller, an attorney representing the Committee to Restore Value at Sallie Mae, said Sallie Mae's proposals still do not offer a "real choice" to shareholders.
The Committee is headed by Albert Lord, who is currently a director of Sallie Mae, along with seven of his associates.

Sallie Mae, whose board consists of 14-elected shareholders and seven appointed directors, had proposed a slate of 18 directors that included Lord and one of his associates, but the two withdrew from consideration.
"We are proposing to let the shareholders have a choice," Mueller said. "We would propose a slate and the company could put their slate up."

"We believe that we put forth a proposal at the board meeting that would have assured that privatization was approved by shareholders as soon as possible and that would have given shareholders a true choice on where this company goes in the future," Mueller said. He said the group now running Sallie Mae "has only made a gesture toward governance and is still seeking to entrench themselves on the board."
Mueller said the special meeting the dissidents are seeking would take place at the same time or before the May 15 meeting the company has called.
In a press release Friday, Sallie Mae said the majority of its directors strongly urges shareholders not to sign or return the Lord group's proxy material.

"Strong board leadership is integral to the board's recommended reorganization plan," said William Arceneaux, chairman of the Sallie Mae board in a statement. "Once adopted, the new governance structure will allow shareholders broad authority to make changes to the board."
He said there was no longer any "any rationale for another special meeting."

In an interview, Gisela Vallandigham, a Sallie Mae spokeswoman, said the company's board slate as it now stands "would be the envy of any institution." She said the Sallie Mae stock price has tripled and profit margins are up.

At the May 15 meeting called by the company, shareholders are asked to approve a plan which would make Sallie Mae a holding company incorporated in Delaware and end its status as a government-sponsored enterprise operating under a federal charter.
